# LoopBridge: Should Prefill and Decode Loop Equally?

> Looped (recurrent-depth) language models use the same number of loops to read the prompt (prefill) and to generate
> each answer token (decode), although generation is almost all decoding. We untie the two loop counts (prefill m
> loops, decode n < m) and introduce LoopBridge (2.4% of parameters on Ouro-2.6B; 0.017-0.25% on 26.4B sparse-MoE
> looped models: cache-foldable prompt KV maps + optional decoder LoRA), a lightweight adapter distilled from the
> full-loop model that folds into the prompt cache once at prefill with virtually zero per-token decode overhead.
> Evaluated on Ouro-2.6B, Ouro-1.4B, Thinking models, Lev decision models, and 26.4B sparse-MoE looped models
> (TML-d24-varloop-research and Inkling-2-Mini) in Day-0 vLLM. Every number is recomputed from released per-item scores
> by ouro/scripts/paper_numbers.py (Ouro) and inkling/make_figs.py (26.4B MoE).

Main findings (95% paired bootstrap intervals in the paper):
- At batch 1 on Ouro-2.6B, prefill is 0.3-2.6% of the wall time of a chain-of-thought request (0.1-0.3% on Thinking models).
- One decode loop (Ouro-2.6B): LoopBridge 4/1 raises the 11-benchmark average from 44.2 (Original 1/1) to 58.2
  (58.3 +- 0.1 over three seeds), above tied-loop distillation on the same data (49.5; rank 80: 49.3); at two decode
  loops, 63.7 -> 69.1 (vs 66.2 Distilled 2/2); MATH-500 zero-shot.
- Measured time (Ouro-2.6B, 800 requests, batch 1): LoopBridge 4/1 scores 45.0% (+17.2 over Original 1/1, +10.8 over
  Distilled 1/1) at 27.7 tokens/s (vs 28.3 for Original 1/1) and +10.5 points over a time-matched Original 1/1-2/2 mix;
  4/2 runs at 14.3 tokens/s (2.1x Original 4/4). At batch 32, LoopBridge 4/1 stays +18.5 / +11.3 points ahead in
  1.18x / 1.19x time.
- The gain peaks within two to five prefill loops (also for an adapter trained to 16 loops, over seeds, and with the
  prefill loops trained too).
- Transfers to Ouro-1.4B (44.5 at 4/1, 44.2 +- 0.2 over three seeds, vs 40.5 distilled and 34.7 original),
  Ouro-2.6B-Thinking (4/2 within 0.8 points of 4/4 on average and +3.1 above Distilled 2/2; served in batches, matches
  Original 4/4 on all 1,319 GSM8K problems at 2.0x throughput and 0.47-0.57x wall time), and Lev decision models.
- Scales 10x to 26.4B sparse-MoE looped models in Day-0 vLLM (TML-d24-varloop-research & Inkling-2-Mini) on five
  official reasoning and 256K-1M benchmarks (GPQA Diamond, LiveCodeBench v6, MRCR v2 8n 256K-512K, GraphWalks BFS 256K,
  LongBench v2 1M; 29 archived 5x avg@4 arms = 124,816 rollouts), separating the two zero-decode-overhead modules:
  * Variable-depth TML-d24-varloop at n >= 2 (22 full 5x avg@4 arms = 94,688 rollouts):
    training-free untying works natively (4/2: 68.4-68.9 vs 66.9 Orig 2/2; 4/3: 73.3-74.0 vs 73.1 Orig 3/3), and
    pure-prompt KV-Only maps (lora_rank=0, 4.46M-6.55M params = 17-25 MiB = 0.017-0.025%, frozen decoder, 0% decode
    overhead) lead both dedicated depths: LB 4/2 KV-Only reaches 69.6% (+2.78 [+0.82, +4.67] 5-Bench, +4.29
    [+1.37, +7.18] 3-Long, +9.54 [+2.91, +16.49] MRCR 512K over Orig 2/2, all surviving k=3 Holm-Bonferroni 98.33% CIs,
    plus +1.99 [+0.25, +3.73] 95% CI on uncloned 1M LongBench v2 [+3.34 [+0.98, +5.78] p=0.0052 on strictly 13-gram-clean
    N=307 vs -0.13 on 196 overlapped items], at 1.75x decode vs 4/4). Complete 4-cell 2x2 causal factorial & matched twins:
    (a) tied KV-Only 2/2 (m=2, 2.36M active) is flat at 67.0% (+0.13), so untying m=2->4 causes +2.65 [+1.14, +4.16]
    5-Bench (p<1e-3; +3.43 3-Long, +5.49 MRCR) on the full corpus; on 12M 0%-nosynth data, matched LB 4/2 0%S (68.7%) vs
    KV-Only 2/2 0%S (68.0%, p=0.13 vs 2/2) gives directional +0.70 [-0.93, +2.27] (p=0.40; +1.90 3-Long p=0.12), exposing
    an m x synth interaction (+1.96 pp), while 0%-nosynth LB 4/2 still beats full-synthetic KV-Only 2/2 by +1.71
    [+0.05, +3.35]; (b) scaling tied 2/2 to full r=64 LoRA (Distilled 2/2, 46.9M, 5.8h) hits 68.9% (tying zero-shot TF
    Tail 68.9%, p=0.98), whereas untied LB 4/2 twins at 12M r=64 (40.6M, 2.13h, 69.6%) and 24M r=128 (66.8M, 69.8%) tie
    9.1-15.0x-smaller r=0 LB 4/2 KV-Only (LoRA-KV: -0.03 p=0.98; +0.17 p=0.81); (c) one single 11.01M (0.042%, 42.0 MiB
    fp32) 0%-synthetic universal adapter (18M tokens = 6M/cell) serves 4/3 (73.8%, 98.6% of 4/4), 3/2 (69.8%, #1 r=0 at
    n=2, +2.93 [+1.39, +4.46] p=0.0004 vs 2/2, +1.79 [+0.42, +3.17] p=0.013 vs 0%-nosynth KV-Only 2/2, +2.34* LBv2
    p=0.0072 vs Distilled 2/2, 25% cheaper prefill), and 4/2 (68.4%) without reloading; (d) in a 3-way closed-form Plato's
    Key test (192 unlabeled prompts), orthogonal 1->1 Procrustes 4/2 (68.4%, 41.9% dark-memory CV) beats Cross-Ridge 4/2
    (60.7%, -7.63*), yet behavioral KL LB 4/2 KV-Only significantly beats Procrustes 4/2 on 3-Long (+2.45*) and MRCR 512K
    (+6.06*, 59.2% dark-memory CV). LB 4/3 KV-Only reaches 74.1% (99.0% of Orig 4/4's 74.9% at 1.27-1.29x decode; 0%S 4/3
    73.5%); both beat Orig 4/4 end-to-end across all lengths up to 262K with 9/9 step-0 & 96.8-97.9% 31-step PyTorch-vLLM
    parity, 1.25-3.58x moderate & saturated async Poisson ITL speedup, and 0 preemptions under tested load.
  * Fixed-depth Inkling-2-Mini 3/2 & un-gated n=1 VarLoop 3/1 (locked 24M, full 5x avg@4): all unadapted n=2 variants
    collapse (Mini TF 3/2 Anchored: 2.2%, 93.2% trunc; Mini Orig 2/2 & TF 3/2 Tail: 5.6% GPQA; Mini Procrustes 3/2: 11.1%
    GPQA, 81.8% trunc; VarLoop TF 3/1: 40.8%), while KV bridge + merged decoder LoRA rescues accuracy and beats
    parameter-advantaged tied distillation on both backbones: Inkling-2-Mini 3/2 reaches 57.7% vs 52.0% Distilled 2/2
    (+5.70 [+4.10, +7.34] 5-Bench, +9.36 [+6.95, +11.84] 3-Long, p<1e-4; 58.3% @1 at 48M v2), and VarLoop 3/1 sweeps
    Distilled 1/1 5/5 (50.0% vs 44.7%, +5.31 [+3.53, +7.14] 5-Bench, +8.50 [+5.83, +11.23] 3-Long, p<1e-4; 3-step KV-map
    ladder 48.9 -> 49.7 -> 50.0 5-Bench and 26.7 -> 29.6 -> 31.4 MRCR [+4.70 [+0.84, +8.53], p=0.017]).
- Multi-turn and agentic serving (1x B300 8-scenario grid, 19-arm BFCL v4 Multi-Turn [15,200 executable episodes], and
  19-arm official zero-Docker SWE-bench Verified [N=50, mini-swe-agent bash-only]):
  * Hardware crossover (1x B300): naive full re-prefill (Policy R, APC off) drops to 0.52-0.75x vs APC 4/4 on short-output
    turns (crossing 1.0x at L_A ~ 256), whereas prefix-cached Policy APC-D0 (83.6-83.7% grid APC, zero dual-KV, 2+2m
    global slots) sustains 1.50-1.76x speedup across all 8 workloads; measured incremental 4-pass prefill bounds analytical
    dual-state Policy I (3+2m+2n global slots + 160-200 MiB SWA/SConv state, unimplemented in vLLM) at 43-105 ms/turn.
  * BFCL v4 Multi-Turn (91.3-91.8% APC): on TML-varloop, APC-D0 preserves Orig 2/2 (46.8% vs 46.5% long_context; 47.9% vs
    48.3% avg) while flipping Policy R by +8.00 [+3.00, +13.00] (p=0.0044, 1.77x) and avoiding Distilled 2/2 LoRA drift
    (+6.25 [+1.50, +11.00], p=0.0124; 1.69x vs APC 4/4), and sweeps effort=low (47.0% vs 44.5% Orig 2/2, 44.0% APC 4/4,
    42.0% Policy R [+5.0*, p=0.0060]). On fixed-depth Mini, Orig 2/2 collapses to 0.0%, APC-D0 rescues to 49.5%/39.2%, and
    Policy R [Policy I semantics] reaches 44.5% long_context (+7.75 [+2.50, +12.75], p=0.0044 vs Distilled 2/2).
  * Official SWE-bench Verified (96.0-96.6% APC, 0 harness errors): at n=2 on TML-varloop, r=0 Universal 3/2 (70.0%, 50.4s,
    1.78x vs 4/4) and LB 4/2 D0/APC-S (68.0%, 50.1-51.4s, 1.75-1.79x) match Orig 2/2 (68.0%, 47.1s, 1.90x) while avoiding
    Distilled 2/2 drift (60.0%; directional +10.0 [0.0, +20.0], p=0.058). At n=1, the 4-policy ladder + matched Distilled
    1/1 (32% Orig -> 40% Dist 1/1 -> 44% D0 -> 46% APC-S -> 70% Policy R [I sem.], +38.0* vs 1/1 and +30.0* vs Dist 1/1,
    p<1e-4) isolates upgrading shallow A_{t-1}. Honest boundary: single-turn Mini LB 3/2 (50-62%) trails Distilled 2/2 (70%;
    -12.0 p=0.032 APC-D0, -20.0 p=0.0036 APC-S, -8.0 p=0.20 Policy R).
- Baselines: the Ouro distilled baselines move by at most 0.9 points over 0.3x-3x learning rates (0.7 at rank 16, 0.9 at rank 80).

Limitations stated by the author: timing on one GPU architecture (B300) up to batch 32; on short-output 128K-256K
prompts (G=512), deeper m-pass prefill attenuates end-to-end speedup relative to shallower-m baselines (though 4/3 and 4/2
still beat equal-m Orig 4/4 end-to-end at 262K); under unconstrained single-stream (B=1) high-effort reasoning on 26.4B
models, n=1 decoders inflate chain-of-thought length by 1.4-1.8x so n >= 2 dominates B=1 wall time whereas n=1 leads in
batched throughput cost; our current vLLM prototype retains 2+2m global KV slots, and exact dual-state Policy I for n=1
(3+2m+2n global slots + 160-200 MiB SWA/SConv state) is analytical/unimplemented in vLLM (accuracy evaluated via Policy R);
single-turn asymmetric LoRA on fixed-depth Inkling-2-Mini trails tied distillation on 40-step SWE-bench bash trajectories
(50-62% vs 70%), motivating multi-turn asymmetric distillation and per-prompt adaptive depth routing.

## Docs
- README.md: findings, 26.4B vLLM single-turn & multi-turn agentic results, quick start, repository map
- REPRODUCE.md: every table and figure -> script -> result file; Ouro and 26.4B vLLM commands
- paper/loopbridge.pdf: the 38-page paper (<=8-page ACL main body + Appendices A-P)
- ouro/results/items/: Ouro per-item scores; ouro/results/paper_numbers.json: recomputed Ouro statistics
- inkling/results/: 26.4B sparse-MoE official-exact avg@4 & avg@1 per-item JSONs, isolated Day-0 vLLM Blackwell timing logs, systems_rebuttal/, multiturn_systems_b300.json, eval_bfcl_multiturn.json, and eval_swebench_verified_n50.json
- ouro/results/provenance/: Ouro run manifests, logs, configs, and checkpoint hashes
- docs/ARCHIVE.md: public ModelScope checkpoints/data (`torushy/LoopBridge`, `torushy/LoopBridge-Data`) and cold-archive notes
- Checkpoints (ModelScope, 16 adapters: 8 Ouro + 8 26.4B MoE): https://modelscope.cn/models/torushy/LoopBridge
- Data (ModelScope): https://modelscope.cn/datasets/torushy/LoopBridge-Data
- docs/DEPRECATED.md: pruned legacy scripts/arms and remaining optional branches
- The tag paper-arxiv points to the exact commit the arXiv PDF and all figures/tables were built from.
